subject: Request: Temporary hold on backup purge for upcoming audit / DPA evidence
messages:
From: Audit Lead <audit@hallowayhealth.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@hallowayhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: temporary hold on backup purge for upcoming compliance audit

Hi Sofia,

We're starting a scheduled compliance audit next month for Halloway Health and our auditors have asked us to provide a stable copy of logs and backups covering the most recent 12 months. We noticed the regular backup/prune cadence for our Redwood tenant would remove several incremental snapshots in early October.

Can Redwood place a temporary hold on the scheduled backup purge for our account until the audit completes (we expect completion by end of Nov, possibly early Dec)? Specifically we need: 
- A 90-day hold on the automatic snapshot deletion for tenant halloway-prod;
- An extract or evidence of subprocessor list + last-mile data flows (S3 buckets, GCS mirrors, any third-party backup tooling);
- A SOC2 excerpt or attestation covering retention and log integrity for the period Jan 2025—Aug 2026.

Procurement is copied for any required paperwork or addenda. If you need an official DocuSign, we can send a request, but we wanted to check feasibility and timing first.

Thanks,
Karen Miller
Lead, Compliance & Audit
Halloway Health
audit@hallowayhealth.com

(attachment: audit-scope-2026.pdf)

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Audit Lead <audit@hallowayhealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@hallowayhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary hold on backup purge for upcoming compliance audit

Karen — thanks for the details and for looping procurement in. We can support a temporary hold, but need to coordinate legal and ops for the exact scope, duration, and required evidence.

Proposed immediate next steps (suggested by me):
1) Legal review: Kimberly, can we draft a narrowly scoped DPA addendum that authorizes a temporary retention extension for halloway-prod only (specifying snapshot IDs and time window) and limits access to audit personnel?
2) Ops action: Ben, can you confirm whether we can pause scheduled purge for that tenant and what the earliest safe resume date is (including any manual rollback steps)? Also call out storage cost delta and risk notes we should include in the addendum.
3) Evidence: Marissa, please pull the current subprocessor inventory and the SOC2 attestation excerpt/redacted copy we can share with Halloway.
4) Customer paperwork: Karen/Procurement — if you can trigger a DocuSign envelope for the addendum once legal confirms language, that will speed sign-off.

I attached a draft DPA addendum template and an ops runbook extract to this thread to accelerate review.

If everyone is OK, I'll put a short timeline in HubSpot and mark the ticket urgent.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
(attachment: DPA-addendum-draft.docx)

Cc: Audit Lead <audit@hallowayhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2026 12:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary hold on backup purge for upcoming compliance audit

Sofia — thanks for the heads up and the draft addendum. A few legal / compliance notes: 
- We can prepare a time-limited, account-scoped addendum authorizing a hold on scheduled deletion for tenant "halloway-prod" only. The addendum should include the exact snapshot date ranges and an explicit end date (we prefer a 30-day extension by default with an option to extend once with documented justification).
- A 90-day open-ended hold is a higher risk for us (storage liability and potential PII surface). If Halloway can justify 90 days in writing (audit start/end dates + why 30-day isn't sufficient), we can consider it.
- Required evidence: redacted SOC2 attestation excerpt is fine, and a CSV of subprocessors + roles (processing, storage, backups) is acceptable. We will not disclose internal operationally sensitive details (e.g., network diagrams).
- Workflow: Ops must enact the hold but we need a written request from Halloway and a signed addendum.

Ben — please provide a short ops impact statement (what changes, how to revert, monitoring requirements) and a target date to resume automatic purging if we implement a hold today.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

On Fri, Sep 25, 2026 at 10:03 AM Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com> wrote:
> Karen — thanks for the details...

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Audit Lead <audit@hallowayhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary hold on backup purge for upcoming compliance audit

Team,

Operationally we can pause the automated purge for the Halloway tenant. Notes below: 
- Technical approach: flip the tenant-specific purge flag and snapshot-retention TTL for halloway-prod. This prevents the automated snapshot lifecycler from deleting the snapshot objects, but keeps normal write/read access.
- Revert path: revert purge flag and run a reconcile job to apply standard TTLs. We have a one-click rollback in our ops console but recommend scheduling the reconcile during a low-traffic window to avoid throttling.
- Earliest safe resume date: if we enact the hold today, we can safely resume automated purge on 2026-12-01 (roughly 65 days) without extra coordination. To support a 90-day hold we'd need explicit written authorization and should budget the storage delta.
- Risks & mitigations: increased storage costs (~$1.6k/month at current snapshot volume for halloway-prod), small increase in snapshot-management surface area; we'll enable stricter ACLs and a read-only audit user for exported evidence to mitigate data-proliferation risk.
- Attachments: ops-purge-runbook-stub.txt (contains the CLI steps, runbook checklist, and rollback commands).

If legal signs off on the addendum, ops can implement the flag change on the same day (we'll require a ticket and signed DocuSign envelope ID).

Ben Carter
Sr. Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
(attachment: ops-purge-runbook-stub.txt)

DocuSign envelope and purchase order coming from procurement@hallowayhealth.com within 48 hours. Once you confirm the DocuSign envelope ID we will expect ops to place the hold. Appreciate the quick turnaround.
